title: Verifier‑Assisted versus LLM‑Only Pre‑deployment Network‑Change Validation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We measured whether adding a deterministic pre‑deployment verifier plus a bounded automated repair budget improves the fraction of intent‑driven network‑change proposals that pass semantic validation compared with accepting a single LLM candidate. In a preregistered paired design (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) we executed 300 paired intents (100 per difficulty stratum) using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic validator. Each pair reused one shared_initial LLM candidate and compared: (a) baseline — accept the single candidate, and (b) guarded — run deterministic validation and allow ≤1 automated repair. Results: baseline 299/300 unflagged passes (0.9966667), guarded 300/300 (1.0); contingency n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; absolute paired difference = 0.0033333; exact two‑sided McNemar p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.01] (bootstrap seed = 1729, B = 10000). The solitary deterministic rescue corrected a sequencing omission via one constrained edit. Under the shared_initial estimand and the chosen synthetic suite the baseline was near ceiling, limiting observable deterministic rescue. We archive preregistration, execution, validator traces, repair trace, and analysis artifacts with the run bundle to enable reproducibility and targeted follow‑ups.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to NetOps tasks such as intent→configuration translation, template synthesis, and automated repair. For pre‑deployment changes, semantic correctness properties—sequencing constraints, reachability, and policy preservation—are operationally critical and cannot be assured by surface syntactic checks alone. A common engineering pattern pairs generative models with deterministic validators and bounded automated repair (generate→validate→repair) to reduce operational risk. However, the measurable benefit of such guarded pipelines depends on what is held fixed (the estimand), the generator single‑shot quality, the validator's expressiveness, and the permitted repair budget.    

We preregistered and executed a paired experiment (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) that isolates deterministic rescue attributable to a validator + bounded repair when the same single LLM candidate is evaluated under two treatments. For each intent the pipeline produced exactly one shared_initial candidate (gpt-5-mini) reused for both conditions: baseline (accept single shot) and guarded (validate and permit ≤1 automated repair). The primary research question: does adding a deterministic verifier plus at most one automated repair increase the probability that a single LLM candidate passes semantic pre‑deployment validation compared with accepting that same candidate without repair? Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered paired evaluation isolating deterministic rescue under a shared_initial estimand; (2) an archived execution and analysis bundle including validator traces and the single automated repair transcript; and (3) an evidence‑grounded discussion of estimand conditioning, ceiling effects, and operational implications for NetOps pipelines.
sections.related_work: Recent surveys and system papers document rapid progress in applying LLMs to NetOps tasks (intent translation, configuration synthesis, test generation, and repair) and note practical tradeoffs between model capability and validation scaffolds [1,3,4]. Tool‑augmented agentic frameworks (planner‑centric and ReAct‑style) enable LLMs to call external validators or simulators to coordinate multi‑step NetOps workflows; these frameworks motivate generate→validate→repair architectures [2,8]. Empirical reports indicate that introducing deterministic checks and generate→validate→repair scaffolds can improve surface correctness relative to unconstrained generation, but effect sizes depend on validator coverage, task distribution, and whether pipelines permit resampling or verifier‑guided regeneration [3,1]. Prior methodological critiques emphasize the need to distinguish benefits from deterministic validation versus benefits from additional model draws or interactive steering; conflating these makes it difficult to bound deterministic rescue attributable solely to post‑generation checking [5,6]. Finally, literature on hallucination detection and deterministic safety nets provides complementary mitigation approaches (entropy or semantic detectors, retrieval augmentation, self‑reflection), though transferability to complex NetOps settings depends on validator design and threat model [7].
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered a confirmatory paired design (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) that defines the primary estimand as the absolute paired difference in the unflagged verifier‑pass proportion (guarded − baseline) on N = 300 paired intents after applying prespecified inclusion/exclusion rules. The main confirmatory test was fixed before observing main‑run outcomes and executed by a frozen analysis executor that reports contingency counts, exact paired inference, and a paired bootstrap percentile confidence interval.    

Task generation and stratification. Tasks were produced deterministically by the registered task generator into a synthetic topology suite stratified into three difficulty levels (low/medium/high). Each task manifest encodes (i) natural‑language intent, (ii) initial and expected final device states, (iii) required sequencing constraints, (iv) preservation invariants, and (v) protected interfaces. The confirmatory run sampled 100 pairs per stratum to produce 300 paired observations.    

Shared_initial protocol, model, validator, and repair operator. To isolate deterministic rescue from resampling benefits we used the shared_initial estimand: for each pair the pipeline produced one shared_initial candidate via the declared generator (gpt-5-mini) and reused it verbatim for baseline and guarded conditions. Semantic evaluation used a deterministic validator implementing full intent‑constraint validation; scoring was binary (unflagged pass vs. flagged). The guarded pipeline permitted at most one automated repair attempt per pair; the constrained repair operator was limited to localized sequencing or insertion edits and was applied only when the validator flagged the shared_initial candidate. Repair attempts were revalidated deterministically; repaired candidates that remained flagged count as failures for guarded in the primary analysis.    

Execution and auditing. The run executed under a scientific confirmatory adapter and completed 600 episodes (300 pairs). Instrumentation recorded model_calls_used = 301 (300 shared_initial generations + 1 repair invocation) and stage counts consistent with the shared_initial protocol. The preregistration specified exclusion rules and a missingness plan; no dual‑call provider outages occurred and no pairs were excluded.    

Analysis procedures. The preregistered confirmatory analysis computed contingency counts (n11,n10,n01,n00), the absolute paired difference, an exact two‑sided McNemar test, and a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (bootstrap seed = 1729, B = 10000). Secondary and stratum tests were designated exploratory and multiplicity‑controlled where reported. All analysis inputs and outputs are archived with the run bundle.
sections.results:
Execution integrity. The adapter completed the confirmatory run with 600 completed episodes yielding 300 paired observations under the shared_initial protocol. Provider/audit records show model_calls_used = 301 (shared_initial = 300, repair = 1). No provider/infrastructure failures or excluded pairs occurred.    

Primary outcomes. Binary scoring produced baseline_success_count = 299 and guarded_success_count = 300 (baseline = 299/300 = 0.9966667; guarded = 300/300 = 1.0). The paired contingency table is n11 = 299, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The exact two‑sided McNemar test on discordant counts returned p = 1.0. The absolute paired improvement is 0.0033333 and the paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (seed = 1729, B = 10000) is [0.00, 0.01]. Because discordance is minimal (m = n10 + n01 = 1) the exact test has limited sensitivity and the bootstrap CI bounds the plausible absolute improvement to at most one percentage point in this experimental context.    

Per‑stratum diagnostics and repair trace. Per the stratification, low and medium strata were at ceiling under both conditions (100/100 each); the sole discordant pair occurred in the high stratum (high: baseline 99/100, guarded 100/100). The single guarded rescue corrected a sequencing omission: the shared_initial candidate omitted a required 'admin down' step before a VLAN/MTU change; the constrained repair inserted the missing sequencing command and the validator then reported an unflagged pass. The repair therefore produced a deterministic rescue with a single additional repair stage call.    

Missingness, contamination, and costs. Contamination checks and negative controls produced no unexpected passes and the missingness summary reports zero failed or unscorable episodes. The guarded pipeline invoked the repair operator once across 300 pairs, so the marginal model‑call cost for deterministic rescue in this run was one additional call (model_calls_used = 301).
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and estimand alignment. Conditioning on a single LLM draw per intent (shared_initial) corresponds to operational policies that limit model calls for latency, cost, or governance reasons. Under such policies the guarded pipeline measures only deterministic validator and bounded repair rescue applied to the same candidate. Workflows that allow resampling or verifier‑guided regeneration change the estimand and commonly increase success rates by exploiting generator variance; those workflows require a different preregistered design.    

Ceiling effects and calibration. The baseline single‑shot generation in this synthetic suite was near ceiling (299/300), producing minimal discordance and limited power to detect small absolute improvements. The preregistration included an optional calibration pilot meant to estimate discordance and inform power; that pilot was not executed. This outcome underscores the practical value of small calibration pilots when generator performance may approach ceiling on chosen task suites.    

Validator coverage and repair budget. The observed rescue addressed a sequencing omission; other failure classes (reachability violations, forbidden ACL removal) were rare or absent in this synthetic distribution. The guarded pipeline’s marginal utility therefore depends on (a) the real‑world distribution of failure modes and (b) validator expressiveness. Expanding validator semantics or repair operators (iterative edits, richer transformations) would change the estimand and likely increase rescue opportunities at additional model‑call cost.    

Operational implications. For deployments that tightly constrain model calls, the shared_initial estimand provides an operationally meaningful bound on deterministic verifier/repair rescue applied to a single candidate. Conversely, organizations that permit multiple calls should evaluate pipelines under estimands that allow resampling or interactive verifier guidance to measure achievable improvements under those policies.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered, archived paired comparison that conditioned on one shared_initial LLM candidate per intent, deterministic validator + ≤1 constrained repair produced one deterministic rescue on 300 paired intents (baseline 299/300, guarded 300/300). The absolute paired improvement was 0.00333 (exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.01]). The result reflects the chosen estimand, the synthetic task distribution, validator coverage, and the limited repair budget. We release the preregistration, execution, validator traces, repair trace, and analysis artifacts with the run bundle to support reproducibility and targeted follow‑up studies that vary estimand conditioning, model strength, task distribution, or repair budget.

limitations: Synthetic benchmark: tasks and topologies were generated by the preregistered deterministic generator; real‑world heterogeneity may expose different failure modes and increase verifier marginal utility.
Single model and validator: only gpt-5-mini and the archived deterministic validator were evaluated; results may not generalize to other LLMs or richer/diverse validators.

Ceiling effect: baseline single‑shot performance was near 100% on this suite (299/300), producing limited discordance and reduced power to detect small absolute improvements relative to larger pre‑specified targets.
Pilot not executed: the preregistered pilot intended for discordance estimation and power calibration was not run; no post‑preregistration power recalculation was performed.

Estimand conditioning: the shared_initial protocol conditions the estimand on a single LLM candidate and therefore does not measure verifier benefit that would arise from allowing independent alternative LLM candidates per condition (resampling or iterative generation).
Repair budget: the guarded condition permitted at most one automated repair per pair; larger or iterative repair strategies may yield different outcomes.
